note.text: African states had diverse post-independence experiences; instability was not a universal or inevitable result of independence. In particular cases, inherited institutional weaknesses, struggles over political inclusion, unequal resource distribution, economic shocks and external interference interacted. Leaders and organised groups also made choices that shaped outcomes. Ethnic identity alone is not a sufficient explanation of conflict. A serious account identifies a mechanism and evidence for a particular place and time rather than treating every country as interchangeable.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain interacting institutional, economic and external pressures without stereotyping a continent. Builds on: different colonial transitions and their unresolved issues. Leads to: military coups and their claimed justifications.

sections.heading: Explain the history
sections.text: African states had diverse post-independence experiences; instability was not a universal or inevitable result of independence. In particular cases, inherited institutional weaknesses, struggles over political inclusion, unequal resource distribution, economic shocks and external interference interacted. Leaders and organised groups also made choices that shaped outcomes. Ethnic identity alone is not a sufficient explanation of conflict. A serious account identifies a mechanism and evidence for a particular place and time rather than treating every country as interchangeable.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: An institutional dispute may concern who can exercise authority; an economic pressure may concern revenue or employment; external involvement may supply support to a faction. These can reinforce one another, but one example does not prove the same chain everywhere. Compare the Congo’s specific crisis with another case instead of presenting a single continental story.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and period before explaining a relationship. Use the practice text only for the claim it supports. Distinguish a cause, an event and an outcome; compare authentic sources before treating an interpretation as established. A sequence alone does not prove that every later outcome was inevitable.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Every political dispute is explained completely by climate alone. Correction: The stated dispute concerns institutions and authority.
Participation and exclusion always mean exactly the same arrangement. Correction: They describe different political relationships.
Economic shocks automatically produce identical coups in every country. Correction: Outcomes depend on institutions, choices and other conditions.
All post-independence conflicts had no international dimension. Correction: Some specific conflicts involved outside powers.
